environments.label: Local dev
environments.topology_summary: Operator-attended provisioning workspace with masked evidence capture and no lawful direct production mutation.

environments.label: CI
environments.topology_summary: Short-lived validation lane where identity assertions stay brokered, candidate-bound, and redaction-safe.

environments.label: Preview
environments.topology_summary: Synthetic review-zone environment with narrowly scoped preview identities and no stable provider trust.

environments.label: Sandbox
environments.topology_summary: First stable provider-enabled rehearsal lane for non-destructive API and callback validation.

environments.label: Staging
environments.topology_summary: Production-shaped verification environment where checkpoint, scope, and environment mismatches must stay explicit.

environments.label: Production
environments.topology_summary: Release-only surface where read-only smoke assertions remain narrow and any grant-bearing flow fails closed.

family_rows.label: HMRC OAuth token bundle
family_rows.summary: User-granted HMRC access and refresh tokens remain vault-bound and may only be proved through masked lineage, never ad hoc taxpayer grant playback.

source_refs.rationale: Raw authority access and refresh tokens live only in the governed secret boundary.
Authority tokens stay bound to the exact client and reporting-subject context.

notes: HMRC taxpayer grant flows are intentionally outside this smoke matrix and remain release-window or operator-attended only.
No raw token outside the governed vault boundary.
Queued sends must revalidate token version before use.

family_rows.label: HMRC sandbox client credentials
family_rows.summary: Sandbox client identity and secret lineage stay attested, environment-bound, and safe for non-destructive token endpoint rehearsal only.

source_refs.rationale: The roadmap explicitly exports HMRC client identifiers and secrets into vault records.
Client identity is a first-class binding input and must remain stable per environment.

notes: Connection method DESKTOP_APP_VIA_SERVER stays bound to cb_sandbox_desktop.
Sandbox and production client secrets must never share one record.

family_rows.label: HMRC production client credentials
family_rows.summary: Production HMRC client material remains export-attested but disabled for unattended grant-bearing smoke execution.

source_refs.rationale: Vault export and rotation evidence apply to HMRC client identifiers and secrets.
Provider environment remains frozen on the authority binding, so live credentials must remain distinct.

notes: Production grant flows require a separate operator-approved release window and never run from the default smoke matrix.
Live authority credentials require stricter approval and rotation evidence than sandbox credentials.

family_rows.label: IdP federation signing and admin material
family_rows.summary: Tenant-admin and signing-key material must prove the intended control-plane tenant without widening runtime client credentials.

source_refs.rationale: Federated identity is a governed security dependency that requires controlled key and admin material.

notes: Do not mix IdP tenant-admin secrets with application client secrets.

family_rows.label: IdP application client secrets
family_rows.summary: Application-client secrets must prove the intended browser and machine client boundaries without exposing raw client material.

source_refs.rationale: Application clients are a provisioning output and therefore create managed secrets.

notes: Separate web, native, and service-principal client material where the IdP does so.

family_rows.label: Email provider API key and sender domain
family_rows.summary: Server-token and sender-domain proof stay environment-scoped, DNS-aware, and lawful for read-only verification only.

source_refs.rationale: The delivery provider account and sender domain create provider credentials and domain-proof artifacts.

notes: Verification state VERIFIED; readiness ACTIVE_AND_RUNTIME_VERIFIED.
Outbound mail identities must remain environment-scoped and redaction-safe.

family_rows.label: Email webhook signing secret
family_rows.summary: Webhook authentication remains explicit, replay-aware, and bound to the expected ingress host instead of provider memory.

source_refs.rationale: Webhook and callback configuration produces shared verification material.

notes: Webhook verification secrets must never be embedded in customer-visible templates or logs.

family_rows.label: Device-messaging server key
family_rows.provider_label: Firebase Cloud Messaging with APNs bridge
family_rows.summary: Push control-plane material must prove the intended project, APNs bridge state, and internal-only delivery scope without sending a live device push.

source_refs.rationale: Device-messaging projects and keys generate platform credentials.

notes: Push payloads must remain redaction-safe regardless of provider choice.

family_rows.label: Error-monitoring ingest token
family_rows.summary: Monitoring overlay credentials stay secondary to first-party telemetry law and may only prove org, project, and ingest posture with masked evidence.

source_refs.rationale: The roadmap provisions error-monitoring project tokens.
Logs and telemetry sinks must redact secrets and full regulated payload bodies.

notes: Error-monitoring vendors must not receive raw authority tokens or unrestricted regulated payload bodies.

family_rows.label: Helpdesk API token
family_rows.summary: Support-provider credentials remain absent until a workspace is explicitly selected; the smoke matrix must preserve that gap instead of inventing a token.

source_refs.rationale: External helpdesk integration requires vendor API credentials when selected.

notes: Support selection status NOT_SELECTED.
External helpdesk sync must not widen visibility beyond customer-safe or operator-authorized context.

family_rows.label: OCR service credential
family_rows.summary: Document-extraction credentials remain blocked until provider choice is explicit and safe metadata-only assertions can be tied to that choice.

source_refs.rationale: Managed OCR projects create provider credentials; self-hosted runtimes require workload identity instead.

notes: OCR workers must not bypass malware-scan or retention controls when fetching source documents.

family_rows.label: Malware scanner credential
family_rows.summary: Scanning credentials remain blocked until the platform or provider decision resolves and a harmless identity assertion can be made.

source_refs.rationale: Managed scanning or self-hosted decision both require governed service identity.
Scan and publish-time visibility checks are mandatory before staged uploads can be delivered.

notes: Scanning credentials must stay partitioned from customer-facing download or preview credentials.

family_rows.label: Vault admin and app auth boundary
family_rows.summary: The secrets-manager admin and app auth boundary is frozen, but live provider choice remains unresolved and must fail closed in the smoke matrix.

source_refs.rationale: Key and secret rotation must be auditable and fail closed on version-binding issues.

notes: Secret-root selection PROVIDER_SELECTION_REQUIRED; root posture LOGICAL_TOPOLOGY_FROZEN_PROVIDER_UNRESOLVED.
Never bootstrap a vault with unmanaged shared credentials embedded in CI or repos.

family_rows.label: KMS root-key admin role
family_rows.summary: Root-key admin posture is serialized, but no live KMS provider is selected yet, so smoke validation must stop at the governed gap marker.

source_refs.rationale: Root key material and rotation are governed at a stronger security boundary.

notes: Root key custody must stay segregated from ordinary application runtime roles.

family_rows.label: Primary DB app and migration roles
family_rows.summary: Database role law exists, but the platform provider is still unresolved, so smoke runs may only preserve alias and role expectations.

source_refs.rationale: Provisioning the primary PostgreSQL store creates runtime and migration credentials.
Migration workflows require a distinct controlled credential posture.

notes: Operational readers must not share write-capable migration credentials.

family_rows.label: Audit-store write role
family_rows.summary: Append-only audit writer credentials remain explicit, but live datastore provider choice is still unresolved and must stay blocked.

source_refs.rationale: Provisioning the audit store creates dedicated credentials or service identities.

notes: Append-only evidence writers should not share mutable control-store credentials.

family_rows.label: Object-storage service role
family_rows.summary: Object-store role boundaries and bucket topology are frozen, but provider choice is unresolved and remains blocked in smoke execution.

source_refs.rationale: Object storage buckets create runtime access roles or keys.

notes: Separate quarantine writers from general artifact readers where the platform allows.

family_rows.label: Broker client auth credential
family_rows.summary: Broker identity remains transport-only and provider-unresolved, so smoke validation must preserve the explicit gap instead of inventing connectivity.

source_refs.rationale: Provisioning a queue or broker creates client-auth material for workers and inbox/outbox adapters.

notes: Broker identities must never imply durable truth ownership by themselves.

family_rows.label: Cache auth token or mTLS identity
family_rows.summary: Cache identity stays strictly non-authoritative and provider-unresolved, so smoke results must keep the block typed and environment-bound.

source_refs.rationale: Provisioning cache and stream-resume state creates service identities.

notes: Cache credentials do not grant access to raw authority tokens or immutable audit evidence.

family_rows.label: OTel ingest identity
family_rows.summary: Collector and backend identity law is machine-readable, but live platform selection remains open and must fail closed.

source_refs.rationale: Provisioning telemetry backends creates ingest credentials or collector trust identities.

notes: Telemetry ingest identities must respect the contract's access separation between operational, security, and privacy signals.

family_rows.label: Registry and signing material
family_rows.summary: The recommended registry and signing stack is encoded, but live provider selection remains pending and the smoke matrix must preserve that governance boundary.

source_refs.rationale: Registry, build-signing, and attestation services create delivery credentials and key references.
Signed artifacts and attestation are release-gate requirements.

notes: Signing keys must remain rooted in the KMS/HSM boundary, not copied into CI runner disks.

family_rows.label: DNS API and cert automation identity
family_rows.summary: Edge control-plane identity is selected and may prove zone, certificate, and preview-domain posture through non-destructive metadata reads only.

source_refs.rationale: DNS, TLS, WAF, and edge delivery provisioning creates domain-control and certificate-automation identities.

notes: Do not reuse DNS or certificate automation credentials as generic deployment credentials.

family_rows.label: CI runner and preview deploy identity
family_rows.summary: CI and preview identities prove subject, audience, broker role, and environment scope without minting broad long-lived delivery secrets.

source_refs.rationale: Runner registration and preview-account provisioning create deployment credentials.

notes: Ephemeral preview credentials must not implicitly grant access to live authority or production secret scopes.

family_rows.label: Apple signing certificate and notary key
family_rows.summary: Apple signing and notarization credentials remain tightly controlled and disabled for unattended smoke execution outside a native release window.

source_refs.rationale: Signed and notarized native delivery requires protected Apple-side signing material.

notes: Desktop-signing material must remain outside general CI runner storage and outside product runtime data paths.

family_rows.label: Desktop update publishing identity
family_rows.summary: Native update-publishing identity remains candidate-bound and disabled outside explicit release windows.

source_refs.rationale: The update channel is a separate publishing boundary with its own release trust.

notes: Publishing identities must only release already signed and notarized artifacts.
